name: C
summary: Learn C syntax, memory, strings, structs, and the standard headers used in everyday programs.

lessons.title: Program entry, types, and output
lessons.explanation: A hosted C program enters main. Declare the type of each variable. An included header makes function declarations available, and printf uses its format string to interpret the arguments.

api.name: printf()
api.description: Format output. Use %d for int and %f for double.

api.name: puts()
api.description: Write a string followed by a newline.

api.name: sizeof
api.description: Determine the size of an object or type in bytes.

lessons.practice: Print the unit price and total on separate lines. Change the quantity and confirm your calculation.
lessons.pitfall: Using the wrong printf conversion for an argument can produce undefined behavior.

exercise.expected: Print a unit price and quantity-derived total on separate lines.
exercise.completion: Changing the quantity changes only the derived total.

lessons.title: Expressions, decisions, and loops
lessons.explanation: An if condition treats zero as false and nonzero as true. Use for when you have a counting pattern and while for a repetition driven by a condition. The remainder operator % is useful for checking divisibility.

api.description: Compare two values for equality or inequality.
Combine conditions with short-circuit evaluation.

api.name: break / continue
api.description: Exit a loop or skip to its next iteration.

lessons.practice: Read one integer upper bound from stdin and sum the multiples of 3 from 1 through that bound.
lessons.pitfall: A single = assigns a value. Use == to test equality.

exercise.expected: Print the sum as a single integer. For a bound below 3, print zero.
exercise.completion: Try a bound divisible by 3, a bound with a remainder, and a bound below 3.

lessons.title: Functions, arrays, and lengths
lessons.explanation: Functions take arguments by value. An array argument normally converts to a pointer to its first element. Pass the number of elements separately so the function knows where to stop.

api.name: size_t
api.description: An unsigned integer type used for object sizes and array counts.

api.name: const int values[]
api.description: Access elements through a read-only view in this function.

api.name: return
api.description: Send the result to the caller.

lessons.practice: Implement a function that counts the even numbers in an array. Pass its length explicitly.
lessons.pitfall: The sizeof array / sizeof array[0] idiom works where the object is still an array. Inside this function values is a pointer.

exercise.expected: Sum a short array without assuming a fixed element count.
exercise.completion: An empty range produces zero and the original array is unchanged.

lessons.title: Pointers, structs, and lifetime
lessons.explanation: A pointer stores the address of an object. Use & to get an address and * to access what a pointer refers to. A struct groups fields of related data. For a struct pointer, -> accesses a field.

api.name: struct
api.description: Define a type containing named fields.

api.name: &value
api.description: Get the address of an existing object.

api.name: NULL
api.description: A macro for a null pointer constant. Check optional pointers before dereferencing them.

lessons.practice: Add a step field and update increment to use it.
lessons.pitfall: Never return a pointer to a local automatic variable. Its lifetime ends when the function returns.

exercise.expected: Add a decrement operation that updates the caller’s counter.
exercise.completion: Increment and then decrement returns the caller’s counter to zero.

lessons.title: Strings and numeric conversion
lessons.explanation: A C string is a sequence of characters followed by a zero byte. Keep track of capacity and choose bounded operations. strtol lets you detect an invalid number or trailing characters.

api.name: strlen()
api.description: Count characters before the terminating zero byte.

api.name: strcmp()
api.description: Compare two strings. Zero means equal.

api.name: snprintf()
api.description: Write formatted output into a bounded buffer. Check its return value for truncation.

api.name: strtol()
api.description: Parse an integer and report where parsing stopped.

lessons.practice: Try the conversion with "42x", an empty string, and a value larger than long can hold.
lessons.pitfall: Arrays storing strings need space for the terminating zero byte.

exercise.expected: Accept a complete base-10 integer token.
exercise.completion: Reject a token with trailing letters and a token outside the range of long.

lessons.title: Dynamic memory and ownership
lessons.explanation: Use dynamic allocation when storage must outlive a block or its size depends on input. Check whether allocation succeeded. Decide which part of the program owns the pointer and free it exactly once.

api.name: malloc()
api.description: Allocate bytes with uninitialized contents.

api.name: calloc()
api.description: Allocate an array and initialize its bytes to zero.

api.name: realloc()
api.description: Resize an allocation. On failure the original allocation remains valid.

api.name: free()
api.description: Release a previously allocated block.

lessons.practice: Allocate space for five scores. Assign each score in a loop and sum them before freeing the array.
lessons.pitfall: If realloc fails, assigning the result directly to the original pointer can lose the only reference to the existing block.

exercise.expected: Read and write valid positions in a dynamically allocated array.
exercise.completion: Check allocation before writing and release the allocation on every path that owns it.

lessons.title: File I/O and cleanup
lessons.explanation: A FILE pointer represents a stream. Check each operation that can fail and close the stream on every exit path. Read text into a bounded buffer with fgets.

api.name: fopen() / fclose()
api.description: Open a stream in a chosen mode and close it after use.

api.name: fgets()
api.description: Read at most capacity minus one characters and terminate the buffer.

api.name: feof() / ferror()
api.description: Distinguish end of input from a stream error.

api.name: perror()
api.description: Print a message associated with the current errno.

lessons.practice: Write two lines to the temporary stream and count the lines read back.
lessons.pitfall: A failed fgets can mean end of input or an error. Test after attempting the read.

exercise.expected: Write and read two short lines in a temporary stream.
exercise.completion: Verify both lines appear in order and check read, write, and close failures.

lessons.title: Integer limits and safe addition
lessons.explanation: C signed integer overflow is undefined. Guard an addition before computing it. This example sums nonnegative counts, so subtracting the second count from INT_MAX is safe after rejecting negatives.

api.name: INT_MAX
api.description: Largest value of int on this implementation.
Evaluate from left to right and stop once an operand is true.

lessons.practice: Guard multiplication of two nonnegative counts. Treat zero as a separate safe case before dividing by either operand.
lessons.pitfall: Checking the sign of a signed sum after it overflows comes too late.

exercise.expected: Report a product only when it fits in an int.
exercise.completion: Check zero, one, two ordinary positive values, and a product larger than INT_MAX.

references.title: WG14 C11 working draft (features used here also apply in C17)

lessons.title: Enums and switch for named states
lessons.explanation: An enum gives a set of integer constants meaningful names. A switch selects one case by value. Returning from each branch is a simple way to avoid accidental fall-through.

api.name: enum State
api.description: Declare an enumeration type and its named constants.

api.name: switch
api.description: Branch to a matching case label.

lessons.practice: Represent a small stopwatch as idle, running, or paused. Decide which transitions are legal.
lessons.pitfall: An enum does not validate data read from a file or entered by a user. Translate and validate external values.

exercise.expected: Translate each known state to a label and reject a pause command when idle.
exercise.completion: Exercise each valid state and at least one invalid transition.

references.title: WG14 C11 working draft (features used here also apply in C17)

lessons.title: Read bounded lines and reject invalid numbers
lessons.explanation: A fixed-size buffer limits each read, but it does not guarantee that an entire line fit. This example expects newline-terminated records and rejects overlong ones. Remove the newline, then pass the field to strtol and check the end pointer and overflow status.

api.name: fgets()
api.description: Read up to capacity minus one characters and terminate the buffer on success.

api.name: strchr()
api.description: Locate the first occurrence of a character.

api.name: strtol()
api.description: Parse an integer and report where parsing stopped.

lessons.practice: Change the producer to emit a malformed integer and an overlong line in separate trials.
lessons.pitfall: If this parser is used in a loop, discard the remainder of a rejected long line before reading the next record.

exercise.expected: Reject incomplete or invalid newline-terminated readings.
exercise.completion: Valid negative text is accepted unless your application prohibits negative readings. A suffix and a line that fills the buffer are rejected.

references.title: WG14 C11 working draft (features used here also apply in C17)

lessons.title: Format into buffers and detect truncation
lessons.explanation: snprintf receives the destination capacity, including room for its terminator. Its nonnegative return value is the length the output would have had without truncation. Check that value against capacity before using the output as a complete record.

api.name: snprintf()
api.description: Format text into a bounded buffer and return the intended character count.

api.name: sizeof label
api.description: Count all bytes of the local array, including terminator space.

lessons.practice: Try a short label and a label much longer than the destination. Print an explicit error when the full value does not fit.
lessons.pitfall: A bounded, null-terminated result can still be a truncated identifier. Treat that as an error when the full value matters.

exercise.completion: Check a label that fits exactly with a terminator and one that requires an extra byte.

references.title: WG14 C11 working draft (features used here also apply in C17)

lessons.title: Sort and search arrays with comparators
lessons.explanation: qsort arranges array elements using a comparator that returns negative, zero, or positive. bsearch uses the same comparison on a sorted range. Comparing with relational operators avoids overflow that would occur if the comparator subtracted two extreme ints.

api.name: qsort()
api.description: Sort objects described by a base address, count, width, and comparator.

api.name: bsearch()
api.description: Look up a key in a range already sorted with the matching comparison.

lessons.practice: Search a sorted list of readings for two keys, one present and one absent.
lessons.pitfall: Binary search can miss existing elements when the array is unsorted or the comparator disagrees with the sort.

exercise.expected: Report a found key or a clear missing result.
exercise.completion: Search the smallest value, an absent value, and an array containing INT_MIN and INT_MAX.

references.title: WG14 C11 working draft (features used here also apply in C17)

lessons.title: Unsigned masks for independent flags
lessons.explanation: A bit mask uses one unsigned bit for each independent yes-or-no option. OR sets a bit, AND tests it, and AND with the complement clears it. A mask of several flags can test all of them by comparing the masked value with the whole mask.

api.name: 1u << n
api.description: Produce a single-bit unsigned mask with a valid shift count.

api.name: flags &= ~mask
api.description: Clear only the bits selected by mask.

lessons.practice: Add an execute flag and report whether both read and execute are set.
lessons.pitfall: Use an unsigned left operand and keep the shift count below its bit width.

exercise.expected: Toggling execute leaves the other flag states unchanged.
exercise.completion: Test all four combinations of read and execute, including both disabled.

references.title: WG14 C11 working draft (features used here also apply in C17)

lessons.title: Headers, separate compilation, and linking
lessons.explanation: A header shares declarations. The compiler compiles each source file into an object file, and the linker resolves references between them. This example puts declaration and definition in one file to demonstrate their relationship. In a larger program, move the declaration to a header with an include guard and the definition to one source file.

api.name: function prototype
api.description: Declare the parameter and return types before a call.

api.name: include guard
api.description: Prevent repeated declarations from a header within a single translation unit.

lessons.practice: Move the prototype into units.h and the definition into units.c. Include the header from the caller and units.c, then run cc -std=c17 main.c units.c -o units in a terminal.
lessons.pitfall: Including a header does not provide the object file containing the corresponding definition. A missing definition is commonly a link error.

exercise.expected: The two-source build produces the same output as the single-source version.
exercise.completion: Build both files and observe 36. Omitting units.c should produce a link error mentioning total_units.

references.title: WG14 C11 working draft (features used here also apply in C17)

lessons.title: Validate command-line arguments
lessons.explanation: A hosted C program may receive argc and argv. argc counts the arguments including the program name when it is available, and argv holds the argument strings. Keep argument validation separate from output so that tests can exercise malformed values independently.

api.name: argc
api.description: Number of supplied argument strings.

api.name: argv[1]
api.description: First user argument, available only when argc is at least two.

api.name: EXIT_FAILURE
api.description: Portable unsuccessful program termination status.

lessons.practice: Remove the teaching default and require exactly one nonnegative argument.
lessons.pitfall: When teaching or testing locally, a default is convenient. In a real CLI, distinguish missing arguments from too many arguments instead of applying the same default.

exercise.expected: Print usage for an incorrect argument count and reject an invalid number with a failure status.
exercise.completion: Try zero, a negative count, trailing text, and a call without a user argument.

references.title: WG14 C11 working draft (features used here also apply in C17)

prerequisites: Know how to save a plain text file.
To run the examples, install a C17 compiler such as Clang or GCC. The reading and exercises work offline.
metadata.miniProject: Build a reading-summary tool. Parse whole-number readings from command-line arguments, reject invalid input, then report a count, minimum, and maximum. Check empty input, the highest valid reading, and a malformed argument.

references.title: WG14 C11 working draft (features used here also apply in C17)
